# StreamDek Mobile — 12 August 2026

## New

**Subtitles look the way you want them to**
Settings → Playback → Subtitles has an Appearance section: text size, vertical position,
bold, and the colour of the text, the background panel behind it and the outline traced
around each character. A preview at the top of the page shows a sample line drawn exactly
as the player will draw it, so a choice can be judged before a film is playing rather than
by reading numbers. Your settings now stay put across videos — size and position used to
reset with every new episode — and the subtitle picker remembers whether you take your
subtitles from the built-in source or from an add-on, so it opens on the list you actually
use.

**Tablet layouts**
The app was a phone app stretched sideways. It is now laid out for the screen it is on:
rows and grids carry more artwork per row, spacing and dialogs scale with the window, and
the profile picker fits the space instead of filling it. Settings opens as two panes, with
the section list beside the page it opens, and a title page in landscape puts the artwork,
title and actions on the left with episodes, sources and cast scrolling beside them — so
choosing an episode no longer means scrolling the poster away first. Rotation is unlocked
above 600dp; phones stay portrait.

## Fixed

**Trailers play, at the quality you asked for**
Trailers stopped mid-scene or never started. The extraction path was being bot-walled and
fell through to a client whose links stop serving after about 8 MiB, and the media host
refuses the open-ended request the player makes by default, answering 403. Both are fixed:
trailers are fetched in bounded spans from a client that is served properly, and the
video-and-audio pair is preferred over the single 360p stream that was being picked
instead, so Trailer Quality under Settings → Appearance → Title Pages now means something.
Titles also open on the actual trailer rather than the first thing in the list, chosen by
running time, so a page no longer greets you with a 15-second theatre sting.

**Hero trailers play once**
A trailer on a title page started again on its own: scrolling the artwork out of view and
back restarted it, and a stream that faulted as it ran out sent it round a second time. It
now plays through once, then the artwork returns. The replay button on the artwork starts
it again whenever you want it, and unmuting is remembered rather than reset with every
trailer.

**Subtitle colours, background and bold reach the player**
Text Colour, Background and Bold Text were saved and shown correctly in the preview, but
the player drew subtitles as if they had never been set — only Text Size and Vertical
Position had any effect. Colours are stored the way Android writes them, alpha first, and
both playback engines were reading those digits in the opposite order: yellow arrived as a
barely-there white, black text disappeared, and the Dimmed Black background was fully
transparent. On mpv two further things were in the way — a background panel was never
drawn at all, and a subtitle that carries its own styling (the ASS and SSA tracks common in
MKV files) ignored everything except sizing, which is why bold appeared to do nothing. Your
choices now override the subtitle's own styling, and a subtitle track is left as its author
styled it while you are still on the defaults.

**The subtitle preview follows the Vertical Position slider**
The sample line sat at the bottom of the preview whatever the slider said. It now moves
through the frame the way it will move over video, and slides off the bottom edge past 100
— the same as it would off the picture.
